title: file-browser: universal file-open dialog with source-provider adapters (open any file; localhost-only)

decisions.text: Adapter architecture in TS/Bun (owner agreed 2026-07-12). A FileSourceProvider interface { id, listRoots(), listDir(path, opts), stat(path), openStream(path) } with a server-side provider registry; the UI selects a provider by id. LocalFsProvider (Bun node:fs/promises) ships first. Future providers (RemoteAgentProvider on another Bun host, DbProvider, WebProvider) plug in as additional ids behind the same UI. FPC-CLI REJECTED: Bun is already the filesystem data-plane (readdir/stat/realpath over WS) and a self-contained per-host agent; the repo's FPC cli/ is a DSP engine and AppMain.exe is a webview host, not a file service. FPC would add a second language + new IPC for a capability Bun already has.

Security = localhost-only, via a SEPARATE 127.0.0.1 bind (owner choice 2026-07-12). The file-browse endpoints (fs.*) listen on their OWN loopback-only socket bound to 127.0.0.1, not reachable over the LAN — chosen over per-message remote-address checks for a harder guarantee that doesn't depend on proxy-forwarded addresses. This replaces the single-root isPathInsideBase sandbox (audio-file-utils.ts:62-90) for the local provider: full-machine read, but only from localhost. Path canonicalization (realpath) is kept to avoid symlink/traversal surprises. The main server keeps serving UI/other endpoints to LAN clients as before; only file-browse is loopback-locked. Transport = HTTP REST on this loopback server (GET /fs/roots, /fs/list, /fs/stat) — chosen over WS since a separate bind is naturally a second Bun.serve and it matches the existing audio HTTP endpoints. The main server exposes GET /api/fs/info (loopback-detected via server.requestIP) so the UI discovers the loopback URL + availability; remote clients get available:false and cannot reach the bind anyway. CORS is permissive on the loopback server (safe: only same-machine browsers can reach it). Remote sources get their own auth as separate providers later.

OS-specific roots, OS-agnostic UI (owner req. 3, 2026-07-12). Provider.listRoots() is OS-aware: Windows -> drive letters (C:\, D:\, ...) plus known folders (Desktop/Documents/home); POSIX -> '/' (plus home and mounted volumes). The UI NEVER hardcodes 'drives' — it renders whatever listRoots() returns as top-level entries (label+icon) and navigates over opaque path strings from the provider. All Windows-vs-unix difference lives inside the provider; the dialog is identical on every OS.

Three view modes (owner req. 5, 2026-07-12): (a) linear LIST — names only, dense; (b) ICONS — small/medium/large sizes; (c) TABLE 'Total Commander style' — columns name/ext/size/mtime/attributes, each column sortable in both directions. View mode + last sort are a persisted UI preference (localStorage). FsEntry carries {name, path, isDir, isSymlink, size, mtimeMs, ext, kind} so all three views + all sort keys work from one payload.

Quick regexp filter, TC Ctrl-S style (owner req. 6, 2026-07-12). An incremental filter box narrows the visible list live as the user types; matches against the entry name. Regexp by default (case-insensitive, toggleable); an invalid regexp falls back to a literal substring match (no error spam). Esc clears the filter and restores the full list. Filtering is client-side over the already-loaded dir payload.

Performance & sorting (owner req. 7, 2026-07-12). listDir returns the full dir payload with metadata (name/isDir/size/mtime/ext) in one pass via readdir({withFileTypes}) + batched stat; sort & filter run client-side for typical dirs, with q-virtual-scroll for large ones. Provider.listDir(opts) reserves optional server-side sort+paginate params for huge dirs (100k+) as a later optimization — not built up front. Directories sort before files by default; sort is stable.

Coexists with the preset browser during migration (owner choice 2026-07-12, REVISED). The universal dialog is invoked from a classic menu bar (File -> Open, FB-D8); the old presetsRoot q-tree STAYS in place for now — the dialog is added beside it, not a replacement yet (full retirement is a later migration step). presetsRoot survives as the dialog's default/initial location. The editor's open path reuses resolveAllowedAudioFilePath's kind-detection, but path authorization shifts from single-root to the loopback bind + canonicalize (FB-D2). Favorites are in scope (FB-D10); image thumbnails are future (Phase 4).

Classic application menu bar (owner req. 9, 2026-07-12). A classic-style top menu bar is added; a File menu with an Open item invokes the universal dialog. This is new UI chrome (Quasar) hosting the entry point for the dialog; further menu items can follow later. The menu bar is where the migration off the q-tree eventually lands (open/recent/etc.).

Editor-supported type filter (owner req. 1 clarified, 2026-07-12). The dialog lists ONLY editor-supported files by default — audio/gnaural extensions (.gnaural/.wav/.flac via getAudioFileKind); directories are always shown for navigation. The provider still walks the whole filesystem; the type filter is applied to the file listing (a filetype dropdown may expose 'all files' later, but the default and primary mode is supported-types-only).

Favorites / bookmarks (owner req. 11, 2026-07-12). The dialog can add sources to a favorites list — folders, files, etc. A favorite is stored as {providerId, path, label, kind:'dir'|'file'} so it generalizes to non-local providers later. User adds/removes a favorite from the dialog (e.g. star/context action); the list persists (localStorage) and shows in a sidebar next to the roots; clicking a favorite jumps to that folder (or selects that file). presetsRoot seeds the list as a default favorite. Distinct from OS-provided roots (FB-D3): roots come from listRoots(), favorites are user-curated.

artifacts: server/fs-browser-local.ts: listRoots OS-aware — Windows drive letters (parallel A-Z probe) + known folders (Home/Desktop/Documents/Downloads); POSIX '/' + known folders + best-effort volumes (/Volumes, /media/<user>, /mnt) (FB-D3)
listDir via readdir({withFileTypes}) + batched stat -> FsEntry[]; dotfiles hidden unless showHidden; parent=null at a root boundary (FB-D6)

evidence: smoke: listRoots -> C:\Users\1 (Home), C:\, D:\ in 3.5ms

steps.title: Separate 127.0.0.1 bind for file-browse endpoints (owner req. 2, FB-D2)
artifacts: server/fs-browser-server.ts: startFsBrowserServer() = own Bun.serve({hostname:'127.0.0.1', port:0}); GET-only /fs/* routes; the main LAN-facing server exposes NO /fs/* routes
isLoopbackAddress() helper (127.*, ::1, ::ffff:127.*) for the main server's /api/fs/info gate
server.ts: fsBrowserServer started before Bun.serve; stopped in disposeAudioSession; boot logs its loopback URL
steps.verify: /fs/* reachable over 127.0.0.1 bind; main server has no /fs routes; isLoopbackAddress accepts loopback + rejects LAN
evidence: fs-browser-server.test.ts: bind url matches ^http://127.0.0.1:\d+$; isLoopbackAddress cases pass

steps.title: HTTP REST wiring on the loopback server: GET /fs/roots, /fs/list, /fs/stat + /api/fs/info discovery
artifacts: GET /fs/roots|/fs/list|/fs/stat carry ?provider=&path=(&hidden=1); dispatch through the registry; permissive CORS (*) + OPTIONS 204; 400 unknown-provider/missing-path; 404 unknown route
main server GET /api/fs/info reports {available, url, providers} via server.requestIP loopback detection (remote -> available:false, url:null)
steps.verify: round-trip over 127.0.0.1: /fs/roots -> /fs/list(root) -> /fs/stat(file); /api/fs/info reports available:true from localhost
evidence: fs-browser-server.test.ts round-trip + CORS + error cases pass
live boot smoke: /api/fs/info -> {available:true, url, providers:[local]}; ${url}/fs/roots returns roots JSON
NOTE: tests strip HTTP_PROXY (dev machine sets HTTP_PROXY=127.0.0.1:2080 which Bun's fetch would route loopback through -> ECONNRESET); real browsers do not proxy own-origin localhost
